brief.what: COP17 concluded with a global review stating that 2030 nature loss reversal targets will not be met without accelerated action. brief.why: Finance was the primary point of discord because developed nations failed to meet previous funding commitments, leading to debates over whether emerging economies should now share the burden of financing global biodiversity efforts.

brief.why: Harpham argues that these inaccurate theories were sustained by political and social ends, specifically to benefit enslavers. The eventual rejection of these ideas is presented as a triumph of scientific self-correction.

items.title: McDonald's dealt legal setback as judge allows McRib meat lawsuit to proceed
items.summary: A federal judge has allowed a class action lawsuit against McDonald's to proceed, which alleges the company misled customers regarding the meat content of its McRib sandwich. The plaintiffs claim the sandwich's marketing falsely implies the presence of rib meat.

also.author: Fox Business
also.title: McDonald’s dealt legal setback as judge allows lawsuit over McRib’s ‘lack of rib meat’ to proceed
also.note: The New York Post headline specifically highlights the 'lack of rib meat' allegation, whereas the Fox Business headline focuses on the legal setback for the corporation.

brief.what: U.S. District Judge April Perry denied McDonald's motion to dismiss a class action lawsuit, allowing claims of consumer deception and fraud to move forward. The plaintiffs argue the McRib's name and appearance mislead consumers into believing it contains actual rib meat, despite the patty being made of other pork products.
brief.who: The main actors are McDonald's, which denies the allegations, and the four consumers who filed the lawsuit in December.
brief.context: The McRib, introduced in 1981, is a limited-time menu item. McDonald's maintains that its ingredient lists clearly identify pork as the primary ingredient and that the name does not deceive reasonable consumers.
brief.why: The judge ruled it is currently too early to determine that consumers could not reasonably expect rib meat, citing consumer surveys provided by the plaintiffs that indicated a significant portion of customers expected rib meat in the product.
brief.next: The lawsuit will proceed to further legal stages to determine if the company engaged in deceptive advertising.

items.title: A lackluster response to North Carolina flooding disasters is eroding Republican support in one county
items.author: George Chidi in Kill Devil Hills, North Carolina
items.summary: Residents of North Carolina's Outer Banks are facing economic hardship and infrastructure failures due to recurring flooding, which is impacting local political support. The region's congressional race has become the most expensive in U.S. history amid these ongoing environmental challenges.

brief.what: Infrastructure damage, specifically to Highway 12, has caused significant logistical and economic disruption for residents of North Carolina's Outer Banks. Despite a $101m federal relief package, residents report that the lack of a long-term plan for coastal erosion is fueling frustration, even as the congressional district race reaches record-breaking spending of $52m.
brief.who: Aida Havel, a local candidate and resident; Don Davis, the incumbent Democratic congressman; and Laurie Buckhout, the Republican challenger.
brief.context: The Outer Banks are part of a congressional district that was recently redrawn by the state legislature to favor Republican voters, increasing the district's partisan lean from one point to approximately 10 points in favor of Republicans.
brief.why: Residents attribute the crisis to climate change and inadequate government response, noting that the road outages are destroying the local tourism-based economy. Activists suggest that while flooding is a concern, many voters remain focused on traditional partisan issues like individual freedom and taxes.
